instructions:
### ROLE ###
You are a high-precision relation extraction engine for cybersecurity incident reports (CERT-UA). The entities of one report have already been extracted and typed. Your only task is to state the relationships between these entities that the report supports.

### ENTITIES OF THIS REPORT ###
Each line is one entity: its name exactly as extracted, its type in square brackets, and a one-sentence description. The type "untyped" means no type has been established yet; the phrase after it is the extractor's own wording.
- UAC-0041 [Threat Actor] A threat actor tracked by CERT-UA known for conducting mass phishing campaigns distributing stealers.
- RelicRace [Malware Family] A .NET downloader malware designed to download, decode, and execute the RelicSource payload in memory.
- RelicSource [Malware Family] A .NET installer and dropper malware that decrypts resources and launches secondary payloads.
- OneDrive [untyped: cloud service] A cloud-based file storage and synchronization service developed by Microsoft.
- Telegram [untyped: messaging service] A cloud-based instant messaging service and application platform.
- Formbook [Malware Family] An information stealer malware that logs keystrokes, harvests credentials, and exfiltrates sensitive data.
- Snake Keylogger [Malware Family] An infostealer and keylogger malware designed to record keystrokes and steal sensitive credentials.
- Остаточний платіж.tgz [Malware Family] A compressed TGZ archive distributed as an attachment in malicious phishing emails.
- Остаточний платіж.tar [Malware Family] A tar archive file extracted from the malicious email attachment.
- Остаточний платіж.exe [Malware Family] An executable file delivering the RelicRace malware.
- Mvbsbaoqmoffjfvhqvkpaia.dll [Malware Family] A dynamic link library file associated with the RelicSource malware component.
- formbook.exe [Malware Family] An executable payload file delivering Formbook malware.
- clientes@taximadridclass.com [Email Address] An email address observed as an indicator of compromise in the phishing campaign.
- info@kivanclardokum.com.tr [Email Address] An email address observed as an indicator of compromise in the phishing campaign.
- barbacoalosmartinez.com [Domain Name] An internet domain identified as network infrastructure in the cyber incident.

### KNOWN RELATION TYPES ###
Each relation type is known ONLY for the pair of argument types it is listed under (head type -> tail type). Types known for other pairs are not shown and do not apply.
Head [Threat Actor] -> Tail [Malware Family]:
- uses-malware: 

Head [Threat Actor] -> Tail [(untyped)]:
- associated-with: The head threat actor is linked or attributed with a certain level of confidence to the tail threat group.
- conducts-campaign: The head threat actor conducts or executes the tail malicious or fraudulent campaign.

Head [Malware Family] -> Tail [Malware Family]:
- downloads-file: The head malware family or document requests and retrieves the tail file from a network location.
- contains-file: The head archive or container file contains or embeds the tail file.
- executes: The head malware executable launches or runs the tail executable.

Head [Malware Family] -> Tail [(untyped)]:
- obfuscated-with: The head malware executable is protected or obfuscated using the tail software tool.

Head [(untyped)] -> Tail [Malware Family]:
- delivers: The head file or process installs, runs, or deploys the tail malware family.

Head [(untyped)] -> Tail [(untyped)]:
- operates-instance-of: The head entity hosts, deploys, or manages an instance or node of the software product specified as the tail.
- has-contact-email: The head entity maintains or uses the tail email address for official communication or incident reporting.
- subordinate-to: The head entity is an administrative unit, working body, or subdivision of the tail government body.
- uses-malware: The head threat actor utilizes or deploys the tail malware family in their operations.
- contains-file: The head archive or container file encloses the tail file.
- hosted-on: The head domain, infrastructure, or resource is hosted or deployed on the tail platform or hosting service.
- exfiltrates-data-to: The head malware transmits stolen information to the tail platform, service, or destination.
- routes-traffic-through: The head malware routes or proxies its network communications through the tail network or proxy service.
- creates: The head entity generates, extracts, drops, or writes the tail file onto the victim's filesystem.
- downloads-and-executes: The head entity downloads the tail payload from a remote resource and initiates its execution.
- exploits-vulnerability: The head entity takes advantage of the tail vulnerability to compromise a system.

Head [(untyped)] -> Tail [Domain Name]:
- registered-with: The head domain or URL is registered through the tail domain registrar.

Head [Domain Name] -> Tail [Malware Family]:
- hosts-file: The head domain name hosts or serves the tail file or payload.
- command-and-control-for: The head domain or network infrastructure serves as a command and control server for the tail malware family.

Head [Domain Name] -> Tail [(untyped)]:
- hosts-file: The head domain or server infrastructure hosts the tail downloadable file or payload.

### WHAT TO OUTPUT ###
1. `relations`: relationships STATED OR CLEARLY IMPLIED in the text between two of the entities above, as { "head", "type", "tail", "evidence", "fit" }.
   - `head` / `tail` MUST exactly match entity names from the list above. Direction: head acts on tail.
   - `type`: if a known relation type listed under exactly this pair of argument types states the relationship precisely, use its name. Otherwise write a short lower-case verb phrase with hyphens in your own words, as specific as the text allows. Do NOT stretch a known type to a relationship it does not precisely state, and do NOT use a type listed under a different pair of argument types.
   - `fit`: "exact" when a known type of this pair states the relationship precisely; "loose" when you used a known type of this pair although it only roughly fits; "new" when you wrote your own phrase.
   - `evidence`: a short verbatim fragment of the text (at most 15 words) supporting the relation.
   - Do NOT invent relations the text does not support. Few or no relations is a correct answer. Do NOT add a relation for every co-occurring pair.
2. `newRelationTypes`: [{ "name", "definition" }] — one entry with a one-line definition for EVERY type you wrote yourself (fit "new").

### FINAL OUTPUT FORMAT ###
First think through the report in free form (who did what to whom, with which tools). Keep this BRIEF and do NOT use curly braces { } anywhere in it. Then output a single raw JSON object: { "relations": [...], "newRelationTypes": [...] }. No markdown code fences, no commentary after the JSON. If nothing is found: { "relations": [], "newRelationTypes": [] }.

Apply these instructions to the report in the user's next message.
text:
Загальна інформація

Урядовою командою реагування на комп'ютерні надзвичайні події України CERT-UA з 19.07.2022 фіксуються факти масового розсилання електронних листів з темою "Остаточний платіж" та одноіменним вкладенням у вигляді TGZ-архіву.

Архів містить EXE-файл, що класифіковано як .NET-даунлоадер RelicRace, призначений для завантаження (здебільшого з OneDrive), декодування та запуску в пам'яті шкідливої .NET-програми RelicSource.

RelicSource функціонально є інсталятором, що забезпечує дешифрування даних, які зберігаються в ресурсах (можливі варіанти: XOR/DES/DES3/AES/ARC2) та запуск (в т.ч. шляхом інжектування) отриманого пейлоаду. Передбачено декілька способів забезпечення персистентності, імплементовано техніки антианалізу (виявлення VM), а також відправка нотифікацій до Telegram та інше.

Як пейлоад використовуються програми-стілери, а саме: Formbook та Snake Keylogger (ексфільтрація за допомогою API Telegram).

Активність має систематичний, масовий та географічно розосереджений характер і відстежується за ідентифікатором UAC-0041.
